owner: authored per-object decisions for Mapillary detections (and the two OSM entrance gates the infrastructure stage already draws); read by scripts/pipeline/compile_representation_plan.py (R-AUTHORED-REJECT / R-AUTHORED-MINIMAP / move_to) via scripts/pipeline/authored_mapillary_decisions.py
derivation_boundary: A decision changes what the plan builds for a detection. It never edits the detection in mapillary_objects/.

decisions.basis: Second sighting of the junction box 488736436076904: same object--junction-box class, same 3 frames, raw positions 1.9 m apart (E 379751.68 N 3938510.82 vs E 379752.56 N 3938509.14), built 0.2 m apart so the two street_cabinet meshes read as one grey slab beside the platform railing (editor top view F_junction_boxes_top_y0.png shows one slab, not two objects). 488736436076904 stays.

Second head of the signal 549495626481668: both are traffic-light detections, raw positions 0.9 m apart (E 379767.76 N 3938493.74 vs E 379766.86 N 3938493.75), same frames; it was built 8.2 m away on the other side of the track (E 379771.09 N 3938495.96, carrier 24475081 chainage 731.6). 549495626481668 stays as the one signal. The generic same-class merge would also fold it; this row records the reviewed decision.

Cabinet (street_cabinet) at the platform edge: built E 379766.71 N 3938488.33, 2.1 m from route 1 and 2.8 m from the station anchor, i.e. on the platform edge line; the raw detection (4.0 m from the built point) is itself 2.0 m from route 0. No position inside the platform clearance is supported by the detection, and the roof above it hides the object in every editor view (F_platform_edge_cabinet_top_y0.png shows only the flat roof), so it is kept off the platform.
